status: Final G03 benefit/cost gate and decision rule; registered before any measured batch (only the n=5 fixture smoke ran).
question: Does route-scoped gzip of Stremio JSON give a repeatable net benefit without LAN/CPU degradation beyond the plan 2.3 common gate?
source: C image + frozen aaa9ee5 server/app overlay (g02-post-cr17-v2 manifest, re-verified by controller).

lan.note: direct Docker internal network, no shaper

workload: Real StremioStreams/MetaResponse/StremioCatalogResponse models via FastAPI response_model under Hypercorn run() defaults; payloads streams 0/1/10/40/200 (40 = normal max path, 200 = stress), series meta with 50 videos, catalog 200 (stress). Upstream cost stubbed constant (prebuilt seeded instances); serialization per request real. Accept-Encoding: gzip on every request.
variants: identity-a and identity-b (noise baseline, same process, interleaved), gzip1/4/6 = Starlette GZipMiddleware minimum_size=1.
thresholds: Candidate thresholds 1/2/4/8 KiB are derived: payloads below T stay identity (identity cells), payloads >= T use gzip cells.
profiles: lan = direct Docker internal network; wan50/wan10/mob2 = shared-bottleneck relay (50/10/2 Mbit/s, 20/40/80 ms RTT). Limit: the relay delays data, not the TCP handshake, so fresh-connection cells do not include handshake RTT (identical for all variants).
sampling: 5 repetitions; per repetition one fresh server per profile; profile order rotated by repetition; variant order rotated by repetition+payload; modes c1/c4/c8 keep-alive and fresh (new connection per request, c1); 100 measured requests per cell after separate warmup.
resources: client 2 CPU on 2,3 / 1 GiB; server 1 CPU on 4 / 512 MiB; relay 1 CPU on 5 / 256 MiB; internal network, no host ports, no outbound, no real credentials.
concurrency_note: Runs alongside G02 (CPU 0,1, until ~17:00) and G04 (CPU 12-14) on disjoint cpusets; shared host may add noise, absorbed by identity-a/b J and range.
metrics: total p50/p95/p99, ttfb p95, server process CPU per request (/__stats process_time delta), wire bytes, client decode time (outside timed window), decoded sha256.
correctness: All 200; identity without Content-Encoding; gzip with Content-Encoding gzip and Vary Accept-Encoding; one decoded sha256 per payload across all variants/repetitions; same server pid per cell; all batches and full row counts. Any failure => INVALID.
decision: Strict plan 2.3 common gate (no CPU/UX budget was designated in writing before measurement). Benefit = median < identity range min - J and >= 2 repetitions below. Repeatable degradation = median > identity range max + J and >= 2 repetitions above. (level, threshold) eligible at a profile iff streams/40 compressed and benefits in all modes at that profile, >= 30 % byte reduction for compressed payloads >= 16 KiB, and no compressed payload shows repeatable degradation of total p95, ttfb p95 or server CPU/request at any profile (LAN included). PASS_CANDIDATE if any profile has an eligible pair (lowest streams/40 c1 p95 chosen); else REJECT_UNDER_COMMON_GATE. Either way the full trade-off table is published; a later budget-based adoption would be a user product decision, not this gate passing.
not_covered: Starlette 1.10.0 GZipMiddleware ignores q=0 (g03-api-preparation): even a PASS_CANDIDATE cannot be implemented with it as-is. Per-variant server memory is not separable (one process serves all variants); process RSS/maxRSS reported only. TLS not covered (packet 24).
validation_before_registration: Assessor run on duplicated smoke data: REJECT_UNDER_COMMON_GATE; with LAN cost and CPU/ttfb artificially neutralized: PASS_CANDIDATE at mob2. Smoke: 0 correctness problems, one decoded sha per payload.
